intro.label: development environment
intro.lead: I build personal projects alongside a full-time job. I use AI tools to speed up execution and a personal VPS to publish applications and learn what happens beyond the frontend. Product direction, requirements, and validation remain my responsibility.

ai.title: More time to build, fewer manual steps
ai.modeLabel: Select an area where I use AI

intro.label: WHY AI
intro.title: An accelerator, not an autopilot
intro.description: With limited time for personal projects, I use AI to reduce repetitive work and speed up research, interfaces, and integrations. Product direction and evaluation of the outcome remain mine.

constraint.label: CONSTRAINT // TIME
constraint.title: Time is a real constraint
constraint.description: Working full-time leaves a defined window to design, build, validate, and maintain personal applications.

ui.title: Turning a visual direction into an interface
ui.description: I define the style, goals, and behavior. AI helps translate that direction into components and layouts, so I can focus on quality before repetitive details.

research.title: Finding my way through technologies and approaches
research.description: I use AI to compare libraries, architectures, and documentation. It narrows the options, then I validate the choice in the project's actual context.

integration.title: Starting integrations that require new research
integration.description: When connecting APIs, services, or less familiar systems, AI helps me explore the problem and prepare an initial solution to verify and adapt.

iteration.title: Leaving more room to evaluate the result
iteration.description: Refactoring and repetitive changes take less time when I can compare alternatives quickly. I use the saved time to check behavior and refine the solution.

infrastructure.title: My projects go beyond localhost
infrastructure.modeLabel: Explore the areas hosted on my personal VPS

apps.title: Applications people can reach
apps.description: I use an IONOS VPS to host web apps and personal services. Its cost-to-performance ratio lets me keep multiple projects online and learn what it takes to run them beyond frontend development.

api.title: Backend services under my control
api.description: Hosting APIs in the same environment gives me hands-on experience with backend processes, service configuration, and communication between frontend and server.

facts.label: PURPOSE
facts.value: APIs and services for personal applications

data.title: Data and continuity are part of the system
data.description: Running persistent data and services makes responsibilities like configuration, backups, security, and service continuity tangible.

experiments.title: A lab for trying real ideas
experiments.description: The VPS is also a place to try automations and small services without turning my local computer into the production environment.

boundary.title: Personal and client environments stay separate

environments.label: PERSONAL // SHARED NODE
environments.title: My VPS
environments.description: My personal environment for applications, services, and experiments that I manage directly.

environments.label: CLIENT // DEDICATED ENVIRONMENT
environments.title: Infrastructure shaped around the project
environments.description: Client projects are not automatically placed on my infrastructure. The environment and deployment depend on actual requirements.

policy.title: Client workloads stay outside my personal infrastructure.
policy.description: Before release, I consider isolation, requirements, infrastructure ownership, and deployment for each project.

environment.title: Tools I keep close at hand

links.title: From systems to projects
links.description: These tools support how I build, collaborate, and bring projects online.
